chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from one who narrated to him, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Imam should remain standing at Jam' (al-Mash'ar al-Haram) until the sun rises, while the rest of the people may hasten (leave) if they wish or delay if they wish.

And it is not permissible to depart from Jam' before the rising of the dawn with choice, and whoever departs before the rising of the dawn intentionally, upon him is the blood of a sheep, and if he was forgetful, there is nothing upon him. He narrated.

key_terms.الْإِفَاضَةُ: Departure or moving from a place, specifically referring to leaving Jam' for Muzdalifah or Mina.
key_terms.الْاخْتِيَارِ: Choice or option, referring to the freedom of the pilgrim to choose their timing.
key_terms.جَمْع: The station of al-Mash'ar al-Haram, a key stop in the Hajr ritual.
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: The blood of a sheep, a sacrificial penalty (dam) for missing a ritual pillar or component due to error.
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: The rising of the dawn, a specific time marker for ritual validity.
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدًا: Intentionally, indicating deliberate action versus forgetfulness.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for leaving al-Mash'ar al-Haram before dawn during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the obligatory stay of the Imam and the discretionary timing for the general congregation at al-Mash'ar al-Haram. It establishes a clear legal precedent where intentional premature departure incurs a sacrificial penalty (*dam*), while forgetfulness exempts the pilgrim, reflecting the Shia emphasis on intentionality (*niyyah*) in ritual obligations.
